subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static military truck model, around 8m long and 3.4m tall, built from boxes and cylinders without joints since it's a static vehicle, oriented to face +Z.

I'm sketching the part layout: chassis rails and crossmembers, six cylindrical wheels with glowing cyan hubs and dark tires, armor-plated wheel arches, and a cab built from an extruded side profile with a sloped windshield, all using a gunmetal and cyberpunk neon color palette.

Still defining windows and windshield geometry...

I'm planning the front details: a bumper with hazard-striped ram plate, cyan headlight bars, and a magenta roof light bar, plus a roof-mounted sensor array with a radar dish and a remote weapon station with twin barrels. For the cargo bed, I'm sketching an armored container with angled side plates.

I'm adding decal planes for an emblem and "2077" text on the door, plus fuel tanks, twin exhaust stacks with glowing tips behind the cab, and a tilted missile pod with angled cylinder tubes on the bed roof.

Now I'm layering in extra details: magenta underglow boxes, mirrors, handles, step ladders, headlight lenses, grille slats, a front winch roller, antenna whips, and red glowing bed lights, with a few cable sweeps between cab and bed. I'm also working out wheel positions and armored wheel arches, calculating the front and rear axle placements relative to the cab and body width.

Centering the tire at x=1.55 to keep penetration hidden, then working out the cylinder geometry for the tire itself and placing tread lug boxes around its circumference using rotation math to position each block at the correct radius and angle.

Adding hub caps, glow rings, and bolt circles for each wheel, mirroring everything for the inner side, and sketching out small helper functions to cut down on repetitive part-creation code.

Adding grille vents with magenta glow, headlight housings with cyan glow boxes, and door panel details on the cab sides including seams, handles, and window glass sections.

I'm checking the window extrusion depth against the cab body thickness to avoid z-fighting, then placing a hexagonal emblem decal on the bed side with glowing "SENTINEL 2077" text, considering how the plane orientation will read from the viewer's angle.

Working through whether the decal text could end up mirrored on one side versus the other, deciding it's a minor risk I can accept given the symmetrical-ish styling of the text.

I settle on using explicit rotation values for each side plane so the text orientation reads correctly from each viewing direction, verifying the math by checking which way the local axes map for both the +X and -X cases. Now I'm sketching the roof details: a radar dish using a flattened cone, a light bar built from a glowing box with end caps, and starting to think through the roof turret shape.

Still placing turret parts... now working out the missile rack geometry on the bed roof, positioning rows of launch tubes with calculated spacing and angled firing directions.

I'm also adding side details to the bed: dark vent slats, thin cyan neon strips along the bottom edges, hazard chevron panels, vertical armor ribs spaced along the length, and a flat panel array plus rear ramp doors with glowing accents on top.

Now I'm positioning the rear tail lights, bumper, and tow bar, then working out the fuel tank cylinders mounted horizontally along the side skirts between the axles, figuring out exact axle spacing and tank placement relative to the wheels.

I'm also laying out the underbody: box-shaped chassis rails, driveshafts, differentials as spheres at the axles, cylindrical axle shafts, and a magenta underglow box with glow strips beneath the chassis. For the cab, I'm adding mirrors with arms and glowing boxes, step plates near the doors, roof hatches, and starting on the exhaust stacks.

Checking the exhaust stack placement, I'm positioning them outside the cab near the bed junction, verifying their radius keeps them clear of the bed sides while still touching the cab at the right height without overlapping incorrectly.

I'm adding a bracket box and a few cable sweeps across the bed roof linking turret to missile using catmull-rom curves, plus some armored brow geometry and slat bars over the windshield. I'm keeping the total code around 350 lines and confirming the turret and antenna heights stay within a reasonable max.

For the wheels I'm writing a reusable function with ten lug nuts arranged around a 14-sided cylinder, then importing a glow kit and texture helper to add emissive highlights to parts like tail lights. I'm also designing an SVG emblem with a hexagon shape and bold monospace "SENTINEL" text, plus a small "MX-77" hazard decal for the door.

I'm checking the geometry so the lug nuts and tire don't sink below the floor plane — settling on a lug center radius of 0.68 with a small negative offset so the overlap stays within an acceptable 2% tolerance of the vehicle's total height.

Now for the lugs, I'm positioning each one by rotating around the x-axis so they sit evenly around the wheel hub, with the bolts offset along the axle. Time to finalize the model and add the hazard stripe details.
